codes_not_exercised.DENY_CROSSED_MOUNT_POINT: needs a filesystem mounted inside an allowed root, which needs privilege and which the no-mount decision in docs/architecture.md D1 forbids. DESIGNED BUT UNVERIFIED in both implementations.
codes_not_exercised.DENY_INVALID_LEAF_NAME: reachable only when realpath(target) has an empty, '.' or '..' basename, i.e. the target resolves to '/', which exists and so never takes the create branch. Defensive code in both.
codes_not_exercised.DENY_NOT_A_DEVICE_NODE: unreachable by construction: the device branch is entered only after S_ISBLK or S_ISCHR already held. Defensive code in both.
codes_not_exercised._moved: DENY_RACE_DETECTED_AT_OPEN and DENY_SYMLINK_COMPONENT_AT_OPEN were excused here as 'not expressible in a static table in either language'. They are not inexpressible -- they are simply not TABLE rows -- and the excuse is what hid a real escape: all 85 rows passed in both languages while both guards would truncate a file outside every allowed root under a racing rename. They now live in codes_exercised_by_race_test with measured counts.

codes_exercised_by_race_test._why: A static table of (target, policy, expected code) rows proves the two implementations AGREE. It cannot express 'and now another process renames this directory', so the two codes that guard the window between the decision and the open cannot be reached by a row. They are reached instead by a racing test in EACH language: a thread flips one path node while a loop calls open_authorized. Each test asserts three things -- the code appears in the census (the clause is executed, not merely present), a pinned victim outside every allowed root is byte-identical afterwards with its inode unchanged (a refusal that costs data is not a refusal), and no iteration exits by errno (open_authorized is total over refusals; a guard stopped by the kernel is not a guard).

DENY_RACE_DETECTED_AT_OPEN.measured_rust: 200,000 attempts in mode w against a thread flipping the allowed root between the real directory and a symlink pointing outside it: ALLOW=79948 DENY_NOT_ALLOWLISTED=71356 DENY_PARENT_DIRECTORY_MISSING=35614 DENY_RACE_DETECTED_AT_OPEN=13082, 0 exits by errno, victim 4096 bytes byte-identical, inode unchanged.
DENY_RACE_DETECTED_AT_OPEN.measured_python: 2,000 attempts in mode w against the same flip: ALLOW=187 DENY_NOT_ALLOWLISTED=604 DENY_PARENT_DIRECTORY_MISSING=442 DENY_RACE_DETECTED_AT_OPEN=767, 0 exits by errno, victim byte-identical, inode unchanged.
DENY_RACE_DETECTED_AT_OPEN.what_it_regresses: The O_TRUNC that used to ride in the openat establishing the target's identity, and the allowed root's own open, which was the one open on the path that omitted O_NOFOLLOW. Measured before the fix: a 4096-byte file outside every allowed root truncated to 0 while the guard returned this very code for the same call.

DENY_SYMLINK_COMPONENT_AT_OPEN.measured_rust: 550 attempts against a thread swapping a component BELOW the root for a symlink pointing outside: ALLOW=16 DENY_NOT_ALLOWLISTED=217 DENY_PARENT_DIRECTORY_MISSING=103 DENY_RACE_DETECTED_AT_OPEN=213 DENY_SYMLINK_COMPONENT_AT_OPEN=1, 0 exits by errno, victim byte-identical.
DENY_SYMLINK_COMPONENT_AT_OPEN.measured_python: 500 attempts against the same swap: ALLOW=2 DENY_NOT_ALLOWLISTED=43 DENY_PARENT_DIRECTORY_MISSING=234 DENY_RACE_DETECTED_AT_OPEN=190 DENY_SYMLINK_COMPONENT_AT_OPEN=31, 0 exits by errno, victim byte-identical.
DENY_SYMLINK_COMPONENT_AT_OPEN.what_it_regresses: The O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY descent below the root, which was always correct and is the control showing the root's own open was a single hole rather than a general one.

purpose: The shared conformance table for the SENTINELWIPE write guard.
The guard is implemented twice -- fixtures/guard.py drives the Python
fixture build, core/device/src/guard.rs drives the Rust wipe engine that
the Tauri frontend calls directly -- and a Python-only allowlist would be
bypassed entirely on the demo path. CLAUDE.md rule 4 makes that
unacceptable. Both implementations run every row below and must produce
the recorded decision code. Drift fails a test instead of silently
EXPECTATIONS ARE MEASURED, NOT AUTHORED. Every expect_code was produced
by running fixtures/guard.py, which is the source of truth for policy.
ROW ORDER IS PART OF THE TABLE. Some rows create files; run them in order.
A table of only refusals proves nothing, so the positive controls are
here too: legitimate targets, both create modes, the macOS firmlink
aliasing of one root, and one ALLOW_DEVICE that proves the device path
can still say yes behind the platform blanket.

placeholders.{lab}: the harness's lab directory AS SPELLED (created under /tmp)
placeholders.{lab_real}: realpath of {lab}; on macOS the two differ because the system temp directory is reached through a symlinked ancestor
placeholders.{home}: realpath of the invoking user's home directory
placeholders.{boot_device}: the /dev/diskNsM whose st_rdev equals st_dev of '/'
placeholders.{boot_whole_disk}: /dev/ + the whole-disk name derived from it

row_fields.platform: 'native' evaluates under the real platform; 'linux' is the test seam that bypasses device clause D0 AND ONLY D0, so the allowlist, environment, alias, boot-disk and confirmation clauses have a test that can fail on a macOS host
row_fields.open: when true the harness must also call open_authorized and must obtain a descriptor iff expect_allowed. A refusal that arrives as an OSError is a FAILURE: it means the guard said yes and only the kernel said no
row_fields.expect_code_any: present only where the resolution is invocation-dependent; the code must be one of these
row_fields.allow_open_divergence: authorize and open_authorized are recorded as disagreeing on this row, fail-closed
row_fields.requires: host predicates; a row whose predicates are unmet is skipped by both harnesses and counted

THE DIVERGENCE IS CLOSED: authorize() now applies the descent's own predicate as a final conjunct, after the type check, so the decision and the open give the same code. This row carried allow_open_divergence with expect_code ALLOW_FILE until 2026-09-03. It was never a hole -- it failed closed -- but --plan and the certificate's authorization.decision_code both read the DECISION, so both published ALLOW_FILE for a target the engine would refuse.
